auditor: four independent Opus subagents, one batch of 25 primaries each in the sample's audit order, reading only the two clones at their pinned tips and their batch - never the product's parse, no ce, no resolver (booklet language-expansion.md section 14 item 14; RG15: assembled verbatim, judgments untouched)

rows.why: The in-tree wrapper sets LUA_PATH=$(CURDIR)/src/?.lua;$(CURDIR)/vendor/?.lua;; (GNUmakefile:67), so src/?.lua finds src/luarocks/core/vers.lua. The installed CLI's prepended luarocks.* searcher (GNUmakefile:85) loads $(luadir)/luarocks/core/vers.lua, a make install copy of that file (GNUmakefile:128-130); the module is already cached at loader.lua:28, before the rocks-tree searcher is inserted (loader.lua:323).

src/?.lua in the in-tree wrapper's LUA_PATH (GNUmakefile:67) finds src/luarocks/fs.lua (there is no fs/init.lua and no vendor/luarocks). The installed build loads its make install copy $(luadir)/luarocks/fs.lua (GNUmakefile:85,128-130), and the test suite puts the checkout's src/?.lua on the path (spec/util/test_env.lua:798-800, :595).

The in-tree wrapper's LUA_PATH $(CURDIR)/src/?.lua (GNUmakefile:67) finds src/luarocks/fs.lua. Installed runs load its make install copy $(luadir)/luarocks/fs.lua through the build's luarocks.* searcher (GNUmakefile:85,128-130).

The luarocks-admin in-tree wrapper sets LUA_PATH=$(CURDIR)/src/?.lua;... (GNUmakefile:75), which finds src/luarocks/util.lua. The installed luarocks-admin's luarocks.* searcher (GNUmakefile:96) loads the make install copy $(luadir)/luarocks/util.lua (GNUmakefile:128-130).

busted runs from the repository root (.github/workflows/test.yml:74-80), and .busted:6 loads this module as the helper before any spec. busted's src/ lpath has no match, and the ./?.lua template (Lua's default path; Windows CI passes --lpath=.//?.lua, test.yml:598) finds spec/util/test_env.lua.

Run from source, the generated wrapper sets LUA_PATH=$(CURDIR)/src/?.lua;$(CURDIR)/vendor/?.lua;; (GNUmakefile:67), so src/?.lua with dots turned into slashes finds src/luarocks/fs.lua; the installed script's first searcher loads $(luadir)/luarocks/fs.lua, the copy make install makes of it (GNUmakefile:85,124-131), the all-in-one binary embeds it from src (binary/all_in_one:192-197,500), and tests prepend src/?.lua (spec/util/test_env.lua:797-800).

Installed build: GNUmakefile:84-85 inserts a first searcher that loadfile()s $(luadir)/luarocks/util.lua, the copy of src/luarocks/util.lua installed by GNUmakefile:128-131; the dev wrapper (GNUmakefile:67, LUA_PATH=src/?.lua first), binary/all_in_one:47 (./src/?.lua) and the test helper (spec/util/test_env.lua:798-800) all reach src/luarocks/util.lua.

Installed build: GNUmakefile:84-85 inserts a first searcher that loadfile()s $(luadir)/luarocks/queries.lua, the copy of src/luarocks/queries.lua installed by GNUmakefile:128-131; the dev wrapper (GNUmakefile:67, LUA_PATH=src/?.lua first), binary/all_in_one:47 (./src/?.lua) and the test helper (spec/util/test_env.lua:798-800) all reach src/luarocks/queries.lua.

Every way luarocks runs maps luarocks.* onto src/luarocks: the in-tree wrapper sets LUA_PATH=$(CURDIR)/src/?.lua;... (GNUmakefile:67), the installed launcher's first searcher loads $(luadir)/luarocks/<name>.lua, which GNUmakefile:128-131 copies from src/luarocks/**/*.lua (GNUmakefile:84-85), and binary/all_in_one:47 uses ./src/?.lua; src/luarocks/fetch/hg.lua exists (the .tl sibling is never on a ?.lua template).

Every way luarocks runs maps luarocks.* onto src/luarocks: the in-tree wrapper sets LUA_PATH=$(CURDIR)/src/?.lua;... (GNUmakefile:67), the installed launcher's first searcher loads $(luadir)/luarocks/<name>.lua, which GNUmakefile:128-131 copies from src/luarocks/**/*.lua (GNUmakefile:84-85), and binary/all_in_one:47 uses ./src/?.lua; luarocks.path maps to src/luarocks/path.lua (distinct from luarocks.core.path and luarocks.cmd.path).

notes: koreader: every entry point requires setupkoenv (reader.lua:22; platform/android/llapp_main.lua:4), and every launcher cds into the install root before running ./reader.lua (platform/*/koreader.sh, make/emulator.mk:10-13), which the Makefile builds by symlinking the repo's reader.lua, setupkoenv.lua, frontend/ and plugins/ (Makefile:56-57,144,155). Both require and dofile rows therefore resolve against the repo layout. The first package.path template, common/?.lua, and the libs/ C libraries are koreader-base build output (base submodule, not checked out; Makefile:136). I could not read it and treated it as shadowing none of the frontend module names. For the bare top-level names (dump, util, logger, gettext, httpclient) I checked that each caller uses API that only the frontend/ file defines; if base did ship a same-named module in common/, those rows would become external. Plugin rows: the loading plugin's root is prepended (pluginloader.lua:242); no plugin root has a same-named file, and no other tracked koreader file ends in the same module path. koreader's test runner ($(RUNTESTS)) and Android's luajit-launcher live in unreadable submodules. For tests, frontend/ is on the path because commonrequire.lua requires frontend modules bare; for Android, setupkoenv's relative templates only work if the working directory is the KOReader root. spore_spec.lua:62 sits in a describe tagged #notest, which the runner presumably skips; it is answered with the file the call loads when the block runs. tools/trace_require.lua redefines the global require only when started with -ltools/trace_require and delegates to the original (line 33), so it changes no answer. luarocks: answers name the in-corpus source file. The in-tree wrappers put src/?.lua first (GNUmakefile:67,75). Installed runs load verbatim make install copies of src/luarocks/*.lua (GNUmakefile:84-85,95-96,128-130), and a bootstrap-installed luarocks rock (GNUmakefile:181-182) is the same files under builtin autodetection (the rockspec has no build table). The .tl twins are Teal sources that no ?.lua template reaches. Every recorded spec was confirmed on its line in live code (not inside a comment or long string), and no batch file rebinds require/dofile/loadfile locally. site_gaps lists real loads in forms a literal-call detector could plausibly miss; I cannot see which sites outside this batch the detector did report.

koreader: resolved with the package.path of setupkoenv.lua:2-4 (reader.lua:22 and platform/android/llapp_main.lua:4 both require it) and the working directory the launchers cd into, the install dir koreader-<target>/koreader/ that symlinks the corpus frontend/, plugins/ and root files (Makefile:56-57,144,155). The first template common/?.lua and the ffi/ and libs/ trees are koreader-base build output (not in the corpus); nothing in the corpus suggests base's common/ holds a frontend module name, so the frontend/?.lua hit is taken as the first in-corpus match. For plugin files, frontend/pluginloader.lua prepends the plugin root while main.lua loads (:242-244), restores the path (:269-270) and appends every enabled plugin root (:285-286); no plugin root shadows any module in this batch, and the same file is reached whether the module is loaded during plugin load or later from package.loaded. commonrequire: the busted lpath for the front suite is set by base/test-runner (submodule, not checked out); the answer rests on the install layout (Makefile:139), the unique candidate and the disable_plugins() call it must satisfy. luarocks: all four run modes (from-source wrapper, installed script, all-in-one binary, busted tests) load src/luarocks/fs.lua or a copy that make install or the binary build takes from it, so the corpus file is the answer. For other batches: Teal-generated luarocks files start with a preamble that may rebind loadfile locally to _tl_compat.loadfile or loadfile (src/luarocks/cmd.lua:1), which is still a file load, not a none site. No row was a mismatch; every row is the only site on its line (nth 0).

koreader: judged against the install layout the project runs from - launchers and the emulator cd into the install dir (platform/*/koreader.sh, make/emulator.mk:10), where Makefile:56/144/155 link frontend/, datastorage.lua, setupkoenv.lua and plugins/ from the repo and Makefile:136 links koreader-base's build output (common/, ffi/, libs/ ...). package.path = the setupkoenv.lua:2-4 prefix (common/, frontend/, plugins/exporter.koplugin/) + the LuaJIT default starting ./?.lua; while a plugin loads, its own dir is prepended (pluginloader.lua:242) and afterwards every enabled plugin dir is appended (pluginloader.lua:285) - no batch module has a same-named file in those plugin dirs. The base/ submodule is not checked out, so I could not list base's common/ directory; I assumed (from its role as third-party library output) it holds no koreader-frontend module names, so frontend/?.lua is the first template that matches for the frontend modules. Every in-corpus answer is the unique in-corpus file with that module name (git ls-files over the whole corpus). luarocks: .lua files only (the .tl sources match no Lua template); every way the project runs (installed wrapper searcher, dev wrapper, all_in_one binary, busted helper) reaches the same src/luarocks file. No row was ambiguous, dynamic, none or mismatch.

Conventions: koreader truths assume the documented run layout, i.e. cwd = the install dir koreader-<dist>/koreader that the Makefile builds by symlinking the repo's reader.lua, setupkoenv.lua, datastorage.lua, frontend, tools (Makefile:56-57,144) and plugins (Makefile:155) next to koreader-base build output (common/, ffi/, libs/, luajit; Makefile:59,136). The first template common/?.lua points into koreader-base output that is not in the corpus; I assumed it holds only third-party modules and never a koreader module name (util, logger, cache, ui/*, document/*). If it did, those rows would be external, but then KOReader's own API calls on those modules would break, so I consider the assumption safe. The project sets no LUA_PATH and no package.preload or custom searcher (git grep), so LuaJIT's default path, which begins with ./?.lua, follows the setupkoenv entries; reader.lua:22 and tools/wbuilder.lua:4 can only find setupkoenv.lua through that cwd-relative template. The busted runner for koreader specs lives in the unchecked base submodule (kodev:659 sources base/test-runner/runtests), so I could not read its lpath; the spec rows rest on make/emulator.mk:35 (tests run in the install dir) and on specs addressing cwd-relative paths. luarocks rows: the wrapper, installed and all_in_one paths all reach the same src/luarocks file. All 25 spec texts occur on their recorded lines with one site per line, so nth 0 fits. Ordinary literal sites next to sampled rows (for example the dofile of flash_ui.lua at frontend/ui/elements/screen_eink_opt_menu_table.lua:18) are not listed as gaps because the batch is a sample. The same pcall(require, literal) form also occurs at plugins/coverimage.koplugin/main.lua:13, but it names android, a module the unchecked luajit-launcher submodule supplies, so it is not an in-corpus gap.
